title: Accessibility: Error and Warning highlights are too similar (especially on dark themes and for Colour-blind Users)
body: ### Tested versions 4.5.1.stable (official) ### System information Windows 11 (64-bit) ### Issue description In the Godot Script Editor, error and warning highlights use very similar brown tones on dark backgrounds. For colour-blind users, these colours are nearly indistinguishable, meaning users like myself cannot reliably distinguish at a glance warnings from errors due to the similar hues and low contrast. This affects Godot's Default theme, Grey theme, and to some extent even Follow System Theme for dark mode users. As shown, warnings and error highlights colour-pick to "brown". Currently these colours are hard coded and not exposed to Editor Settings -> Interface -> Theme (or Accessibility) Please consider adding either user definable hues, or more contrasting/brighter red and yellow highlights as an option. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open any script in the Script Editor 2. Add a line like ``` func _process(delta): pass ``` (you’ll get a warning: “delta is never used in the current function”) 3. Add a syntax error, e.g. remove indentation or misspell func. 4. Observe the line highlight colours for the warning and the error. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) any script: ``` func this_is_an_error() func this_is_a_warning(delta): pass ```
